claims.text: In SQLite WAL mode, changes are appended to a separate WAL and a transaction commits when a commit record is appended, without requiring the original database file to be updated at that moment.

claims.text: A WAL reader keeps a fixed end mark for its transaction, allowing readers to coexist with an appending writer, while SQLite still permits only one writer at a time.

claims.text: Checkpointing copies committed WAL pages back into the database but can be prevented from completing by long-running or continuously overlapping readers, causing the WAL to keep growing.

evidence.locator: Write-Ahead Logging → Checkpointing; Avoiding Excessively Large WAL Files

claims.text: PostgreSQL MVCC gives each SQL statement a snapshot of data so it can see a coherent database version despite concurrent transactions changing underlying rows.

evidence.locator: PostgreSQL 18 §13.1 Introduction

claims.text: Ordinary MVCC reads do not conflict with write locks, but this does not eliminate write-write waiting, explicit locks, or concurrency failures when transactions target the same data.

evidence.locator: PostgreSQL 18 §13.1 Introduction
PostgreSQL 18 §13.2.1 Read Committed

claims.text: Under Read Committed, each SELECT sees the committed database state as of that query's start, so successive statements inside one transaction can see different committed data.

evidence.locator: PostgreSQL 18 §13.2.1 Read Committed

claims.text: Under Repeatable Read, a transaction keeps a stable snapshot from its first non-control statement, while conflicting later updates can cause the transaction to abort with a serialization failure.

evidence.locator: PostgreSQL 18 §13.2.2 Repeatable Read

claims.text: Serializable adds monitoring for dangerous read-write dependencies and can reject a transaction when the concurrent result cannot match any serial execution, requiring application-level transaction retry.

evidence.locator: PostgreSQL 18 §13.2.3 Serializable

claims.text: PostgreSQL MVCC snapshots and SQLite WAL reader snapshots should remain separate concepts: both stabilize what a reader sees, but one is multiversion row visibility and the other is a WAL end-mark mechanism.

evidence.locator: PostgreSQL 18 §13.1 Introduction

claims.note: This scope boundary is project synthesis comparing two database concurrency mechanisms; PostgreSQL documentation does not discuss SQLite WAL.
